1. How a subscriber gets the code
- Built: the code goes in this email, one per person, through a single new SendGrid custom field, `jp1_code`.
- The draft that uses the field: /Users/kenneth/Library/Application Support/Claude/side-session-notes/local_120b7ae4-455f-4969-ab29-1246e7b02a33/jusprin1-loyalty-email-draft.html

2. Where they enter it
- Built and agreed by Kenneth: "Go with this option. Also, currently the billing page is served from the server anyway, right? If this is the case, why do we need an app update in order to do it? the coupon code is being asked on the chargebee checkout page, right?"
- The path in the app:
  1. Click the gear, then "Get more credits". This opens the Credits and plans sheet.
  2. Under the plan cards: "Got a code in our email to existing subscribers? Enter your code".
  3. A page titled "Keep the price you pay now" opens, with a "Code" field and a "Continue" button.
  4. Two cards appear. Their buttons say "Subscribe to Hobby yearly" and "Subscribe to Hobby monthly".

- The $41.99 subscriber's code shows Hobby yearly at $41.99 a year and the same $6.99 monthly.
- These prices never appear on the regular Credits and plans page.

4. What checkout charges, and when
- Built.
- The code takes 100% off the first period. They pay $0.00 at checkout.
- The free period is a fixed full year or month from the day they check out. It is not tied to their JusPrin 1 renewal date.
- The first real charge comes one period after checkout. On the staging checkout, made on 25 Nov 2026, it read "Next charge on November 25, 2027 $59.99".
- After that they pay the loyalty price for as long as they keep the plan. The page says: "You pay for Hobby what you pay now, for as long as you keep it."

The plan has changed in a way that means rewriting most of the email. I no longer move anyone by hand. Each subscriber gets a one-time code in the email. In JusPrin 2 they click the gear, then "Get more credits", then "Enter your code", and check out for Hobby at their old price, with the first year (or first month) free. This works on staging and isn't on production yet.

**What the email has to change:**

1. **The "To keep your price" paragraph gets replaced.** It currently says "Within a day, I'll move your subscription" and "JusPrin 2 first bills you on [their JusPrin 1 renewal date]". Both are now wrong. The new paragraph gives their code and the three steps to use it. It also says the first year or month is free, so they pay nothing today, and that the code works once, until 28 February 2027. Their first charge comes one full period after checkout, not on their JusPrin 1 renewal date. The loyalty session's draft already has this text.
2. **The line about adding a card goes away.** Chargebee's checkout asks for a card or PayPal, so there's nothing left for you to decide there.
3. **"You won't pay twice" now depends on you.** It now reads: "Once you've signed up, I'll stop your JusPrin 1 subscription from renewing on [date]." Someone has to run the `jusprin1_pending_moves` command every day and end each listed subscription at the end of its term. Nobody has been assigned to that yet. If it slips, a subscriber's JusPrin 1 renews and charges them, and that charge needs a manual refund. The first monthly renewals are 7 and 10 December.
4. **A new SendGrid field.** The new field holds each person's code, so the email can't go out until the live codes exist. The subscriber who pays $41.99 gets their code from a separate batch.
5. **The name "JusPrin 1".** You said existing subscribers have never heard the name "JusPrin 1", and the app's code pages already avoid it. The email uses it in the subject, the opening, the "far better" line, the install notes and the footer. I propose the same treatment here, for example "the JusPrin you use now". The subject would become "JusPrin 2 is out, and you keep the price you pay now".
6. **The 500 free credits line stays.** The server gives every new account 500 credits, and they expire one month after sign-up.
7. **Two special cases get simpler:**
   - The subscriber who already has a JusPrin 2 account has no plan there, so they can use a code like everyone else. The separate version of the email for them is no longer needed.
   - The subscriber who cancelled shouldn't get the "I'll stop your subscription from renewing" sentence, since theirs already won't renew. Under the code plan, using the code is how they tell you they want to keep paying, which matches what you asked for.

Before I put the text into SendGrid, I'll check in the app that the gear is where the steps say it is.

**What has to happen before the email can go out, each needing your go-ahead:**

- Move production to the new server image, `obi.4140`.
- Create the loyalty plans, the coupon and the codes on live JusPrin 2 Chargebee.
- Fill in each subscriber's code in SendGrid.

**Subject:** JusPrin 2 is out, and you keep the price you pay now

**Preview line:** Your code to keep your price is inside.

Hi,

You subscribe to JusPrin, so I wanted to tell you myself: JusPrin 2 came out last week, and you can keep the price you pay now.

When a print fails, take a photo and show it to JusPrin 2. It works out what went wrong and which settings to change. You can also just tell it how you want a part printed, and it sets up the slice for you.

Here's a short video of it:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=4NJm0vyzxA8

Once you've used JusPrin 2 for a few prints, I don't think you'll want to go back. But that's your call to make.

Your code: **[code]**

It gets you JusPrin 2's Hobby plan at the [$59.99 a year] you pay now, for as long as you keep it. Hobby is [$100 a year] for everyone else. Your first year is free (your first month, if you pick monthly), so you pay nothing today. Hobby comes with 750 credits a month, doubled to 1,500 until 31 January 2027. Like every new account, you also get 500 free credits for your first month.

To use it:
- Install JusPrin 2 and sign up in it. Use this email address if you can, so I can match you up.
- Click the gear, then Get more credits, then Enter your code at the bottom.
- Type your code and pick yearly or monthly. Checkout asks for a card or PayPal, which is charged only when the free year or month ends.

The code works once, until 28 February 2027.

You won't pay twice. Once you've used your code, I'll stop your current JusPrin subscription from renewing on [21 September 2027]. You keep it until then, and nothing more is charged or refunded for it.

If you sign up for JusPrin 2 with a different email address, reply and tell me which one, so I know which subscription to stop. If you've already bought a JusPrin 2 plan, reply too, and I'll sort it out.

Before you install:
- On Windows and Mac, JusPrin 2 replaces the JusPrin you have now. The first time it starts, it offers to import your printers, with their filaments and print settings.
- JusPrin 2 has its own accounts, and your old chats don't carry over.

Download JusPrin 2: https://github.com/TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin/releases/latest

The announcement has the details: https://www.obico.io/blog/introducing-jusprin-2/

Thanks for supporting JusPrin from the start.

*Footer:* You're getting this because you subscribe to JusPrin.

content.text:
The cold reader got the gist on one skim: JusPrin 2 is out, the code keeps their price, and the first year is free. It said the offer felt mostly like a favour. Three things made it hesitate, and one of them made it suspicious.

**What the cold reader tripped on:**

1. **"You start with 500 free credits" made it suspicious.** It didn't know what credits are, and it wondered whether its subscription still covers the AI. In its words, it "reads like pay-per-use is coming."
2. **It couldn't tell what it would pay, or when.** It read "the $59.99 a year you pay now" next to "first year is free" twice. It also guessed that "check out" means entering a card today, and the email doesn't say so. The words "if you choose monthly" made it ask what monthly costs.
3. **It didn't know what happens to the time it has already paid for.** It read "won't renew" and wondered whether it loses those months, or whether it has to cancel the old plan itself.
4. **Smaller points:**
   - "Once you've used JusPrin 2, you won't want to go back" read as salesy. Next to "replaces the JusPrin you have now", it sounded like it *couldn't* go back.
   - "Get more credits" seemed an odd place to enter a subscription code.
   - "Thanks for supporting JusPrin from the start" felt like a form letter to someone who joined a year ago.

**Proposed revision (only the changed parts; the rest stays as before):**

> As a thank-you for subscribing, the code below moves your subscription to JusPrin 2. Your first [year] is free. After that, you pay the [$59.99 a year] you pay now, for as long as you keep it, instead of the [$100 a year] everyone else pays. Checkout asks for a card, but nothing is charged until your free [year] ends.
>
> Your plan includes credits for the AI: 1,500 a month until 31 January, then 750, plus 500 extra to start. A message to the AI uses 1 credit, or 5 with the Expert model.

> To use it:
> - Install JusPrin 2 and sign up with this email address.
> - Click the gear at the top right of the Home screen, then Get more credits. At the bottom of that page, click Enter your code.
> - Enter your code and check out.
>
> The code works until 28 February 2027. Your current subscription runs to the end of the time you've already paid for, then stops, so you never pay for both.

> Thanks for supporting JusPrin.

**What each change does:**

- **The first-period sentence names only each person's own period.** Yearly subscribers read "year" and monthly subscribers read "month", so nobody wonders about the other price. That needs one more SendGrid field.

"""Lists the JusPrin 1 subscribers whose JusPrin 1 plan has to be ended by
hand: each live JusPrin 1 subscription whose Obico account shares an address
with a JusPrin 2 account that now has a plan, most often the loyalty plan the
subscriber's email offers (JUSPRIN_V2_LOYALTY_OFFERS). Until it is ended,
JusPrin 1 renews and the person pays twice.

End each one on Obico's Chargebee site at the end of its term, never now:
ending now writes a refundable credit for the unused part. A JusPrin 1
subscription already set to end (non_renewing) is counted, not listed.

Then the loyalty plans no JusPrin 1 subscription shares an address with: a
subscriber who signed up for JusPrin 2 with another address, or someone else
who was given the code. Read only; run it once a day while the emails go out."""
from datetime import datetime, timezone

import chargebee
from allauth.account.models import EmailAddress
from django.conf import settings
from django.core.management.base import BaseCommand

from app.accounts import users_by_email
from app.models import Syndicate
from jusprin.ledger.billing import is_loyalty_plan
from jusprin.ledger.ledger import active_v2_plan
from jusprin.models import JusPrinPlan

JUSPRIN_V2_SYNDICATE = 'jusprinv2'


def _day(when):
    if not when:
        return '-'
    return (when if isinstance(when, datetime) else datetime.fromtimestamp(when, tz=timezone.utc)).date().isoformat()


class Command(BaseCommand):
    help = 'List the JusPrin 1 subscribers who now have a JusPrin 2 plan, whose JusPrin 1 has to be ended by hand'

    def handle(self, *args, **kwargs):
        jusprinv2 = Syndicate.objects.get(name=JUSPRIN_V2_SYNDICATE)
        live = [plan for plan in JusPrinPlan.objects.filter(plan_id__in=settings.JUSPRIN_V1_PLANS,
                                                            user__syndicate__name='base').select_related('user')
                if plan.is_active]
        rows, ending, matched = [], 0, set()
        for v1 in live:
            obico = v1.user
            # The Obico account's addresses, and whether the account owns each:
            # an unverified one may belong to someone else, so its match needs
            # the person to confirm from both addresses.
            addresses = {obico.email.lower(): False} if obico.email else {}
            for address in EmailAddress.objects.filter(user=obico):
                addresses[address.email.lower()] = addresses.get(address.email.lower(), False) or address.verified
            for address, verified in sorted(addresses.items()):
                for account in users_by_email(address, jusprinv2):
                    v2 = active_v2_plan(account.id)
                    if v2 is None:
                        continue
                    matched.add(account.id)
                    sub = chargebee.Subscription.retrieve(v1.external_id).subscription
                    if sub.status != 'active':
                        ending += 1
                        continue
                    rows.append([address, 'verified' if verified else 'UNVERIFIED on Obico', f'obico user {obico.id}',
                                 f'JusPrin 1 {v1.external_id} {v1.plan_id} renews '
                                 f'{_day(sub.next_billing_at or sub.current_term_end)}',
                                 f'jusprin2 user {account.id}',
                                 f'{v2.plan_id}{"" if is_loyalty_plan(v2.plan_id) else " (NOT a loyalty plan)"}'
                                 f' since {_day(v2.current_term_start)}'])
        for row in rows:
            self.stdout.write('\t'.join(row))
        unmatched = [plan for plan in JusPrinPlan.objects.filter(
            plan_id__in=[plan_id for plan_id in settings.JUSPRIN_V2_PLANS if is_loyalty_plan(plan_id)],
            user__syndicate=jusprinv2).exclude(user_id__in=matched).select_related('user') if plan.is_active]
        if unmatched:
            self.stdout.write('Loyalty plans with no JusPrin 1 subscription at the same address:')
        for plan in unmatched:
            self.stdout.write('\t'.join([plan.user.email, f'jusprin2 user {plan.user.id}', plan.plan_id,
                                         f'since {_day(plan.current_term_start)}']))
        self.stdout.write(f'{len(live)} live JusPrin 1 subscriptions; {len(rows)} to end at the end of the term; '
                          f'{ending} already ending; {len(unmatched)} loyalty plans unmatched.')

What it does:

- **When it runs:** every day at about 8:04 AM, starting tomorrow. It only runs while the Claude app is open. If the app is closed at 8 AM, it runs the next time the app opens.

That line means nobody has moved yet, so there's nothing for you to do today.

Here's the summary line piece by piece:

- **"19 live JusPrin 1 subscriptions"**: 19 people are still paying for JusPrin 1. That includes the one who has already cancelled, because their subscription runs until 8 August 2027.
- **"0 to end at the end of the term"**: no JusPrin 1 subscriber has a JusPrin 2 plan yet, so there's no subscription for you to end. The email only went out about an hour before this check.
- **"0 already ending"**: no one who moved had a JusPrin 1 subscription already set to stop.
- **"0 loyalty plans unmatched"**: no one has used a code with an address the check couldn't match.

It behaved as designed: nothing to act on, so no notification. On a day someone moves, the "to end" count goes up, and you get a notification naming the subscription and its renewal date.

**One subscriber didn't get the email.** It's 19 subscriptions but only 18 emails. The 19th person pays $6.99 a month, renews on 18 December, and already has a JusPrin 2 account with no plan. I left them out of the upload when the plan was to move everyone by hand, because they were meant to get their own version of the email after you moved them. The code plan replaced that, so right now they have no email and no code. There were only 18 codes, one per person emailed, so they'd need a new one from the monthly batch.

Should I ask the loyalty session to make one more code, then send this person the same email?
but you told me 18, not 19

You're right. I told you 18 without saying it was 18 of 19, and that was my mistake. There have been 19 paying JusPrin 1 subscribers all along. I left one out of the upload on 24 November, because under the earlier plan you'd move that person by hand and they'd get their own version of the email. When the plan changed to codes, I didn't put them back. So every "18" after that, including "sent to all 18 paying JusPrin 1 subscribers", left this person out without saying so.

To fix it, this person needs:

1. **A code.** The loyalty session would create one more on live JusPrin 2 Chargebee, from the regular batch: $59.99 a year or $6.99 a month.
2. **The same email.** I'd add them to the SendGrid list with their code, and send them the same email as a one-person campaign.

They renew on 18 December, so there's time, but not a lot. Should I fix it now: get one more code made and send this person the same email?

I would delete only the batch 5 list. "Delete All Contacts" would also remove the 19 JusPrin 1 subscribers, and with them the open and click records for today's email.

**Already asked, still waiting on you:**
- **The guessable live coupon** `jusprin1-move-first-term`. Its id is easy to guess, and anyone who guesses it gets a free first Hobby period. Archiving it closes that.
- **The test of whether batch 4 did better because of its audience or its email.** I proposed sending batch 4's text and batch 5's text, split at random, to about 9,350 Obico users last active 30–270 days ago. You haven't said whether to build it.

**Not tested: a code entered in the app on production.** The rollout session checked a live code directly through Chargebee: checkout showed $0.00, and the code stayed unused. Nobody has signed in to the app on production and entered a code, because that means creating a production account, which you haven't approved. I also haven't clicked through the gear → Get more credits → Enter your code path myself. I took it from the app's source and the staging screenshots. The first subscriber to use a code will be the real test. The daily check will show whether it worked.

**Cleanup, each waiting for your yes:**
- **In SendGrid:** the test list and test campaign from the subscriber email check, an old test segment, the GlockApps test campaigns, and the empty batch 5 segments. Separately, the one-person test contact k@obico.io holds the fake code JP1-TEST-ONLY, which is harmless.
- **On staging:** a test account and an unused test code from the loyalty session's walkthrough.

**Not done: counting JusPrin 2 sign-ups for each of the four batch 5 groups.** This is the other half of judging batch 5. Opens and clicks are already saved.

**Checked and fine:** the loyalty plan's server code (tsd-enterprise commit `65dd4972f0`) is on both `master` and `release`, so nothing is stranded on a side branch.
